I'm writing an essay on dreams within stories, and I'm wondering if anyone has a suggestion for a book on the subject. I'm currently watching The Matrix and taking notes. I'm going to begin reading Alice In Wonderland and other works by the same author. A book that examines how stories use dreams would be a great help.

Well I am an avid reader, but I am prejudiced against reading about someone's dream. I'm sure it adds something to the plot, but actually whatever it adds can also just be left out and we can get on with what actually happens in the story. That's what interests me, what actually happens. I skip the dream sequences.

A lot of good writers say to avoid dreams in fiction because it basically halts the advancement of the plot elements, same thing with flashbacks (unless they directly add something relevant to the present time plot).

I generally agree with this. It can be done but it's tricky, and the primary thing is to make sure it advances things in the non-dream world in some way. If it doesn't, it's basically superfluous and readers will be itching to get back to the real plot.

I tend to agree with that, but in addition to using a dream as a plot device, I want to explore the concept of dreams in stories on a larger scale.

How does the narrator in Fight Club function when his dreams are stripped away, figuratively and literally via insomnia. How does Neo handle "waking up" from the matrix, and how does his journey inform the morality of that universe? What sort of themes does Lewis Carol explore by placing Alice IN Wonderland? What sort of symbols does Jung focus on when he writes on dreams, and what greater meanings do these symbols hold? What exactly informed The Brothers Grimm version of the collective cultural dream in the early 19th century? In Requiem For A Dream, what sort of nightmare have the protagonists built for themselves, and what does that say about the nightmare we can all construct without careful consideration? Why did Phillip K. Dick ask, "Do Androids Dream Of Electric Sheep", and what greater questions did he answer in that story?
